title: Uzbek Plov
description: One pot, built in layers and never stirred once the rice goes in: lamb browned hard, onions and matchstick carrots cooked down into a broth, then rice steamed on top until every grain is separate. Turned out onto a platter for eight.
notes: Cut the carrots by hand. It is twenty tedious minutes and it is the difference between plov and orange rice pudding — a box grater turns them to mush in the broth.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.note: cut by hand into matchsticks, never grated

ingredients.name: long-grain rice
ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: papery outer skin rubbed off, left whole

steps.text: Heat the sunflower oil in a heavy casserole until it shimmers, then brown the lamb hard in two batches so the pan never cools.
steps.tip: This is the only part of the recipe that wants a loud pan. Everything after it is quiet.

steps.text: Return all the meat, add the onions, and cook until they have gone golden and sweet at the edges.
Add the carrots and let them soften without much stirring — they should still be recognisable batons when the dish is finished.
Stir in the cumin seeds, coriander seeds, salt and black pepper, then pour over the boiling water and scatter in the chickpeas and raisins.
steps.tip: Boiling water, not cold. Cold water drops the pan out of the browning you just paid for.

steps.text: Bury the whole garlic heads in the pan and let this base simmer uncovered until the liquid tastes strongly of everything in it and has reduced by about a third.
Level the rice over the top in an even layer. Do not stir it in — from here the two halves cook separately, one boiling and one steaming.
steps.tip: Add boiling water if needed so it sits about a finger's width above the rice, no more.

steps.text: Cook uncovered until the surface liquid has gone, then poke five or six holes down to the base with the handle of a wooden spoon.
steps.tip: The holes let the steam up through the grain instead of pooling underneath and boiling the bottom layer.

steps.text: Mound the rice into a dome, cover the pot tightly, and steam on the lowest heat you can manage.
Rest off the heat, then turn the whole thing out onto a wide platter, with the meat and the softened garlic sitting on top.
